statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be written in Latin script and be distinctive; non-French names are acceptable only in Latin characters and, when required for statutory documents, must be accompanied by a French transliteration; all constitutional and registration filing documents must be drafted in French.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Greffe rejects the corporate name for lack of distinctiveness or use of prohibited tokens: (i) obtain the written rejection stating legal grounds; (ii) file a rectified dossier without new fees; (iii) if the rejection persists, file an application before the President of the competent Tribunal de Commerce within two months of the rejection notice; (iv) alternatively, initiate a trademark opposition action at INPI if the conflict arises from a pre-existing trademark. France has no stand-alone name reservation procedure; the name is protected from the date of filing at the registry for a practical reservation window of up to 30 days.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), including the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and, for non-established businesses, the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE). Official portal: impots.gouv.fr. Business registration data and SIREN/SIRET identifiers are administered through the national business formalities portal (Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises), operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), with INSEE assigning the SIREN and SIRET identifiers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the SAS and file the formation formalities through the Guichet unique; the filing generates the registration record and enables INSEE allocation of the SIREN and establishment-level SIRET. 2. Obtain the French tax registration notice and identify the competent SIE based on the registered office or establishment. 3. Register for corporate income tax and applicable VAT obligations with the SIE through the professional tax account on impots.gouv.fr. 4. Request or validate the French intra-Community VAT number, generally formatted as FR plus a two-character control key and the nine-digit SIREN. 5. A foreign entity without a French establishment must register with the SIEE where it carries out taxable transactions requiring French VAT compliance; it must provide constitutional documents, foreign tax-registration evidence, proof of activity, identification of representatives, bank details where requested, and transaction or contract evidence. 6. For intra-Community transactions, validate counterpart VAT numbers through the VIES system and file the applicable European sales lists and VAT returns. 7. Maintain separate records for corporate income tax, VAT, customs, payroll, and regulated pharmaceutical-logistics obligations. A French SAS generally does not use a separate federal-style TIN; the SIREN identifies the legal entity and the French VAT number identifies it for VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) by default. Subject to statutory eligibility conditions, certain SAS entities may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu) for up to five financial years, including requirements relating to size, ownership, activity, age, and shareholder participation. This is not a general United States-style check-the-box election. France does not provide a broad entity-classification election allowing an ordinary SAS to elect unrestricted pass-through treatment. Hybrid mismatch, anti-hybrid, controlled foreign company, interest limitation, and treaty anti-abuse rules may restrict the tax effect of contractual or cross-border classification differences.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or TVA), supplemented by customs duties and, where applicable, excise taxes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No single general VAT-registration threshold applies to a French SAS carrying out taxable transactions outside the small-business franchise. The principal French domestic franchise thresholds are generally EUR 85,000 for supplies of goods and accommodation and EUR 37,500 for services, with increased thresholds generally of EUR 93,500 and EUR 41,250 respectively, subject to statutory conditions and legislative changes. A business exceeding the applicable threshold loses the franchise and becomes liable under the relevant rules. A non-established business may be required to register and account for French VAT from its first taxable French transaction, subject to place-of-supply rules, reverse charge, special schemes, and the applicable EU small-business scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting for businesses established in France. All businesses must be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance obligations apply progressively, with large and medium-sized businesses from 1 September 2026 and small and micro-businesses generally from 1 September 2027, subject to legislative or regulatory amendments. Domestic B2B invoices must generally pass through an approved private platform, known as a Plateforme de dématérialisation partenaire (PDP), or another legally permitted public infrastructure arrangement. France does not generally operate a universal real-time pre-clearance or digital-stamp system for ordinary domestic invoices. Transaction data and payment-status data may be reported electronically to the tax administration under e-reporting rules, particularly for certain international and B2C transactions. Public-sector invoices are generally processed through Chorus Pro. VAT invoices must contain mandatory legal particulars, support the applicable VAT treatment, and be retained for the statutory period.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption with the right to deduct input VAT if the exporter can substantiate that the goods physically left the EU customs territory and that the exporter or an authorized intermediary completed the export formalities. Required evidence normally includes the electronic customs export record and exit result, export MRN, commercial invoice, transport documentation, and proof linking the goods to the transaction. Intra-Community supplies of goods may qualify for the French VAT exemption where the customer is VAT-identified in another EU Member State, the goods are transported from France to that Member State, and the supplier holds the required customer VAT number and transport evidence. Freight and logistics services require separate place-of-supply analysis. B2B services are generally supplied where the business customer is established, with customer-side reverse charge where applicable; they are not automatically treated as exports merely because the customer is foreign. Special rules apply to transport, intermediary, warehousing, import-related, and services connected with goods. A French VAT refund requires valid purchase invoices, a deductible business purpose, correct VAT invoicing, and compliance with reporting and limitation rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration and export Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs exit confirmation or equivalent electronic proof that the goods exited the European Union customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the exporter, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and VAT treatment
Packing list and transport documentation, including bill of lading, airway bill, consignment note, or equivalent freight evidence
Proof linking the exported goods to the invoice and shipment, including carrier or freight-forwarder records
Export accompanying document or other customs movement evidence where applicable
Evidence of the customer's location and, for intra-Community supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number
VAT return, accounting ledger, and reconciliation supporting the exemption or deduction claim

Inward remittance evidence where relevant to commercial substantiation; France generally does not impose a universal requirement for an inward remittance certificate as a condition of export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline applicable to ordinary commercial export proceeds. Export VAT exemption or deduction may be denied or clawed back where the taxpayer cannot prove the physical export, customer status, transport, customs exit, or correct place of supply. The DGFiP may assess unpaid VAT, statutory late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, and penalties generally ranging from 10% for certain filing or payment failures to 40% for deliberate breaches and up to 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abusive concealment, subject to the applicable procedure and facts. Incorrect VAT refunds may be recovered with interest and penalties. Serious intentional tax fraud can generate criminal exposure, including imprisonment and substantial fines under the French Tax Code. False customs declarations or misuse of export evidence may also trigger customs recovery, administrative penalties, seizure, loss of customs simplifications, and criminal sanctions. The taxpayer must preserve accounting, customs, transport, invoice, and electronic evidence for the applicable statutory audit period, commonly at least six years for VAT accounting records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank; foreign-exchange policy is principally governed by European Union law, French financial legislation, the French Treasury, the Autorité de contrôle prudentiel et de résolution, and the Autorité des marchés financiers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is in the euro area and the euro is freely convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to EU and French anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, sanctions, tax, customs, prudential, and statistical-reporting requirements. A French SAS may generally receive foreign investment, hold foreign-currency accounts, purchase foreign currency, pay non-residents, repatriate profits, make intercompany payments, and remit dividends without a general exchange-control approval. Dividends require distributable profits, valid corporate approval, withholding-tax analysis, beneficial-owner documentation, and applicable treaty or EU relief. Interest, royalties, management fees, and other related-party payments require contractual support, transfer-pricing evidence, commercial substance, withholding-tax analysis, and arm's-length pricing. Banks may require transaction-purpose evidence, ultimate-beneficial-owner information, sanctions screening, tax-residence forms, and supporting invoices before executing or releasing funds. Certain foreign investments in protected French sectors may be subject to prior French foreign-investment authorization; ordinary GDP pharmaceutical freight and logistics activities are not automatically within a protected sector, but regulated healthcare, critical infrastructure, data, or strategic-supply-chain activities require a specific review. Cross-border cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more carried by individuals entering or leaving the European Union require customs declaration, and cash transported within France may be subject to declaration and evidentiary requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no universal deadline requiring exporters to convert foreign-currency receipts into euros. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign currency or be converted at the company's discretion, subject to the bank's account terms, sanctions controls, AML controls, accounting rules, VAT and customs documentation, and applicable statistical or balance-of-payments reporting. Export declarations, transport records, customer invoices, proof of delivery, and customs evidence should be retained to substantiate the underlying trade. Banks may request prompt receipt allocation and supporting documents under risk-based transaction monitoring, but such bank procedures are not a statutory surrender rule.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment accounts, collection, foreign-exchange conversion, cards, and SEPA transfers, provided the provider is an EU-authorized electronic-money institution or payment institution and is properly passported or otherwise authorized to provide services in France. An offshore digital EMI without EU authorization, French passporting, or an appropriately regulated correspondent structure cannot lawfully provide unrestricted French payment-account services. An EMI account is not a substitute for a French bank account where a capital deposit certificate, statutory escrow, lender covenant, regulated client-money structure, or bank-specific verification is required. EMI safeguarding, payment limits, settlement cut-offs, de-risking, account closure, and limited credit or trade-finance capabilities should be assessed before primary reliance. Client funds must not be commingled with company operating funds where the provider's terms or applicable safeguarding rules prohibit it.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch for corporate-account opening. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified or compliant electronic identification, video verification, certified corporate documents, and beneficial-owner verification. In practice, the bank may require a director, authorized signatory, or ultimate beneficial owner to attend physically or complete a live video interview, particularly for a newly incorporated SAS, non-resident ownership, complex group structures, foreign directors, high-risk countries, unusual payment flows, cash-intensive activity, or pharmaceutical and healthcare-related logistics. A capital escrow account is subject to the selected bank's acceptance procedures and normally requires the incorporation documents, draft articles, shareholder funding evidence, identity verification, and proof of the origin of funds. The company should maintain a French registered office, operational substance evidence, a documented management mandate, and a French-language or bank-acceptable compliance file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to identify or verify the ultimate beneficial owner, ownership chain, control rights, or authorized signatories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles of association; Kbis extract or pending-registration evidence; shareholder register; organizational chart to the natural-person beneficial owners; passports or national identity documents; residential-address evidence; board or shareholder resolutions; powers of attorney; and a signed beneficial-owner declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, parent company, or beneficial owner located in a jurisdiction subject to enhanced sanctions, tax transparency, corruption, or AML concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full group chart; certificates of incorporation and good standing; tax-residence certificates; passports and address evidence for each relevant individual; sanctions and politically exposed person screening results; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; audited financial statements; banking references; and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the French SAS.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of incorporation capital, shareholder loans, intercompany funding, or expected treasury inflows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or shareholder-loan agreement; board approvals; investor bank statements; audited accounts; sale or financing documents where relevant; tax filings; wire-trail evidence from the originating regulated bank; and a funds-flow memorandum identifying each payer, purpose, currency, and beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business description does not reconcile with expected payment volumes, counterparties, routes, currencies, or pharmaceutical-logistics risk profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan; customer and supplier profiles; operating countries; lane and route map; forecast monthly transaction matrix; sample contracts and invoices; freight-forwarding and carrier arrangements; warehouse and temperature-control evidence; GDP-compliance documentation; insurance certificates; customs and transport registrations; and payment-purpose coding procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulated pharmaceutical or clinical-logistics activity appears to be conducted without required licenses, registrations, quality systems, or responsible personnel.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Applicable French and EU authorization analysis; GDP-compliance evidence; competent-authority registrations or licenses where required; quality manual; standard operating procedures; temperature-monitoring and excursion records; qualified-person or responsible-person appointment evidence where applicable; subcontractor qualification files; and a matrix separating freight services from wholesale distribution or other regulated activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, dual-use, restricted-goods, embargo, or high-risk destination exposure in pharmaceutical, medical, or freight transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented sanctions-screening policy; screening logs for customers, suppliers, vessels, banks, owners, and destinations; product classification; export-control analysis; customs documents; end-user and end-use statements; route controls; escalation records; and evidence that blocked or suspicious payments are not processed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected use of cash, personal accounts, third-party payers, nested payment providers, crypto-assets, or unexplained pass-through transactions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash-minimization policy; approved bank-account list; third-party-payment approval procedure; counterparty verification; reconciliations; invoice and delivery evidence; payment-chain diagrams; prohibition of personal-account use; crypto-asset risk assessment; and documented escalation and rejection controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax, VAT, customs, transfer-pricing, or permanent-establishment inconsistencies affecting the stated cross-border model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: French tax registration evidence; VAT registration and filing profile; customs EORI evidence where applicable; intercompany agreements; transfer-pricing policy; logistics-service agreements; permanent-establishment analysis; management-accounting records; tax-residence certificates; and reconciled revenue and payment forecasts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dormant or newly incorporated SAS with no French employees, premises, customers, contracts, or operational evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-office agreement; lease or warehouse contract; employment or contractor documentation; director-management evidence; customer letters of intent; supplier contracts; insurance; regulatory applications; implementation timetable; budget; and board-approved operational launch plan.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route paid-in capital to the designated French bank capital account or capital escrow account from an account held in the name of the subscribing shareholder or investor at a regulated financial institution. Use a payment reference identifying the French SAS, subscription or shareholder-loan instrument, investor name, and capital or funding purpose. Provide the bank with the executed subscription agreement, draft or final articles, shareholder resolution, beneficial-owner information, certificate of incorporation or registration evidence, origin-of-funds documents, and sender-account proof. After registration and release of funds, reconcile the bank certificate, share issuance, accounting entry, and corporate records. For shareholder loans or intercompany funding, use a documented agreement, arm's-length terms, transfer-pricing support, withholding-tax analysis, and a clear principal-versus-interest allocation. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated third parties, anonymous payment intermediaries, or unapproved fintech wallets. Incoming international transfers may use SWIFT MT103; EUR transfers within SEPA should use the relevant SEPA credit-transfer format and include accurate IBAN, BIC where required, originator, beneficiary, and purpose data. Maintain evidence for bank AML review, French accounting, tax, audit, and any applicable statistical reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro suppliers and SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA or foreign-currency settlements. For documentary or higher-risk shipments, use an irrevocable commercial letter of credit, preferably confirmed where bank and country risk justify confirmation, with clearly defined Incoterms, presentation documents, expiry, shipment period, inspection requirements, insurance, transport document, commercial invoice, packing list, customs evidence, and GDP or temperature-control documentation where relevant. Use bank guarantees, standby letters of credit, or documentary collections only under approved credit and sanctions procedures. Match each payment to an approved purchase order, contract, invoice, delivery or freight record, customs document, and verified beneficiary bank account. Apply dual authorization, segregation of duties, callback verification for bank-detail changes, sanctions screening, beneficiary-name validation, payment-limit controls, and reconciliation of freight, customs, VAT, and supplier liabilities. Avoid third-party settlement unless documented, commercially justified, and pre-approved by compliance. For regulated or restricted products, confirm export-control, import-control, customs, and pharmaceutical-distribution requirements before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards entered into with an authorized credit institution or appropriately regulated investment firm, supported by an identified commercial exposure and documented treasury policy
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity management and currency conversion, subject to counterparty limits, confirmations, collateral terms, and accounting treatment

Currency options, including plain-vanilla purchased calls or puts and approved collars, used for documented commercial exposures and subject to suitability, valuation, premium, and governance controls

Non-deliverable forwards only where the reference currency, counterparty, settlement mechanics, and applicable EU and French financial-services rules permit the transaction; NDFs generally settle in a convertible currency and must not be used to circumvent exchange controls or sanctions

Cross-currency swaps for longer-term intercompany or financing exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, confirmation procedures, collateral terms, counterparty-credit limits, and hedge-accounting analysis

Natural hedging through matching foreign-currency receipts and payments, currency-denominated procurement, and centralized netting, provided intercompany pricing, documentation, and tax requirements are satisfied

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential court injunction and daily penalty payment; prolonged non-compliance may support management liability or judicial measures. No automatic strike-off solely for late approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual financial statements, management report and related documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the INPI Single Window
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after approval, or within 2 months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit may trigger a EUR 1,500 civil fine, increased for repeat violations, court injunctions and daily penalties. No fixed automatic strike-off deadline; prolonged inactivity may lead to administrative removal from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and financial statement schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company; otherwise within 3 months after financial year-end, subject to electronic filing rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest at 0.20% per month and possible tax audit measures. Persistent non-compliance may lead to enforced assessment and collection proceedings, not an automatic strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return CA12, if operating under the simplified VAT regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the second business day after 1 May for a calendar-year company, or within 3 months after the financial year-end for a non-calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest at 0.20% per month and possible tax enforcement. No automatic corporate strike-off; VAT registration and tax compliance may be subject to administrative restriction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual CFE local business tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally payable by 15 December each year; amount depends on the municipality and taxable rental value or minimum assessment base
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment may trigger a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest, followed by enforced collection. CFE is a tax rather than a filing fee and does not itself cause automatic strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SAS exceeds at least 2 of 3 thresholds at the relevant assessment date: EUR 5 million balance sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional mandatory appointment rules may apply to certain parent, subsidiary or controlled-group structures.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) rules applies to individual statutory accounts. IFRS may apply to qualifying consolidated accounts or where legally elected.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require a standalone annual UBO confirmation. The SAS must maintain accurate beneficial-owner information and file changes through the INPI Single Window generally within 30 days after a change, including a shareholding or control transfer that changes the beneficial owner.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and corporate officers
Minute Book and register of shareholder decisions
Register of share transfers and movements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 600-2,400 per year; a registered office is required, but France does not generally require a separate statutory registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-15,000 per year for a small or mid-sized SAS, depending on turnover, group reporting, inventory, controls and GDP-related operating complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises may apply the 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profits for a 12-month period if turnover excluding VAT is no more than EUR 10 million, capital is fully paid up, and at least 75% of the capital is held by individuals or qualifying companies meeting the ownership condition. The standard 25% rate applies to the remaining profits. Other incentives depend on eligibility and activity; no general tax holiday applies to a French SAS. A special 3.3% social contribution may apply to IS due, subject to statutory exemptions and a EUR 763,000 allowance.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward under French domestic law; annual use is generally capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. A limited one-year carryback may be elected, subject to a EUR 1 million cap. The five-year value specified in the requested schema does not describe the French rule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD for the IS return, with either the normal-regime schedules 2050-SD through 2059-G-SD or the simplified-regime schedules 2033-A-SD through 2033-G-SD, as applicable. File electronically through the Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP) professional tax account, using EDI-TDFC through an authorized provider or the available online filing service. A French SAS generally files annually.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual IS return; IS installments are generally paid quarterly, with statutory exceptions for qualifying newly formed or small-liability companies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is due within three months after the fiscal year-end. For a fiscal year ending on 31 December, the statutory filing date is generally the second business day after 1 May, with the applicable electronic filing deadline and any officially granted extension to be confirmed for that year. The IS balance is generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end; for a 31 December year-end, generally 15 May. Quarterly installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, subject to the first-installment rules and exemptions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2065-SD, company identification and regime boxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS's legal name, SIREN, registered address, tax office, fiscal year dates, applicable tax regime, and relevant options or status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French-registered SAS's own SIREN and French tax account. Disclose foreign parent or shareholder information in the relevant schedules; do not substitute the foreign parent's tax identifiers for the SAS's.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the taxable result and IS calculation, including any applicable reduced-rate band, credits, reductions, and tax payable. Reconcile the return to the statutory accounts and required tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French SAS's worldwide taxable result under French rules, subject to applicable treaty allocation and French law. Do not exclude foreign-source income solely because the shareholder is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete the applicable balance sheet, profit and loss account, fixed-asset, depreciation, provisions, maturity, shareholding, and tax reconciliation schedules. Use the normal or simplified schedules according to eligibility and the regime in force.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose related-party balances, cross-border transactions, foreign branches, shareholdings, and foreign taxes in the relevant schedules. Maintain source records and currency-conversion support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report distributions and relevant income allocation information required by the form, including dividend distributions and applicable withholding-tax reporting.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify non-resident recipients and apply domestic withholding rules or a properly substantiated treaty or EU exemption. Keep beneficial-ownership, residence, and entitlement evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2572-SD and IS installment and balance payment references
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use the applicable payment references and electronic payment process for IS installments and the final balance. The payment form and reference may vary with the electronic tax account and applicable filing process.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment remains the French SAS's responsibility. A non-resident shareholder does not replace the company's payment obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: File the statement where statutory conditions apply, including the relevant categories and thresholds for specified overhead expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same reporting tests to expenses paid to foreign related parties or service providers; retain invoices, business-purpose evidence, and transfer-pricing support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: File where the statutory turnover or gross-asset threshold, or qualifying group relationship, triggers the French transfer-pricing declaration requirement. Report prescribed information on the group and transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include qualifying cross-border related-party transactions and the required group information. A foreign parent does not remove the French entity's filing obligation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: A late or missing return generally triggers a 10% surcharge, rising to 40% after a formal notice is not remedied within the applicable period and potentially 80% in cases such as concealed activity or abuse of law. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Further penalties can apply for inaccurate declarations, omitted information, or failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation; rates and consequences depend on the violation, notice history, and applicable provisions. Electronic-filing or payment failures may also produce specific surcharges.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Generally 25% on dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate shareholder, subject to statutory exemptions, EU law, and an applicable tax treaty. A qualifying EU parent company may obtain an exemption under the French implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, subject to ownership, holding-period, tax-status, anti-abuse, and documentation conditions. Domestic law may also provide relief for qualifying non-EU corporate parents meeting statutory conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide the French payer with the prescribed residence and treaty-entitlement documentation, commonly including Form 5000-SD and, where relevant, Form 5001-SD for dividends, certified by the competent foreign tax authority. The payer applies a reduced treaty rate or exemption only where conditions are established and should retain evidence of beneficial ownership and entitlement. If full withholding has occurred, the recipient may generally claim a refund using the prescribed French reclaim procedure and supporting residence, payment, and entitlement documents. Confirm the relevant treaty, protocol, anti-abuse provisions, and filing deadlines for the recipient's country.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound royalties are generally subject to 25% French withholding tax when paid to a non-resident, subject to treaty relief and applicable EU rules. Interest paid to a non-resident is generally not subject to French withholding tax, but a 75% rate may apply to payments to a person or entity in a non-cooperative state or territory, subject to statutory exceptions; other special rules may apply. Treaty rates are country- and payment-specific and must be verified against the applicable treaty and protocol. EU directive relief, where relevant, requires satisfaction of ownership, tax-status, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, and procedural conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: French full transfer-pricing documentation generally applies where the French entity or relevant group entity has annual turnover excluding tax or gross assets of at least EUR 150 million, or meets specified ownership or control links with an entity meeting the threshold. The simplified annual declaration obligation under Form 2257-SD has a comparable EUR 150 million threshold and qualifying group-link triggers. Master-file requirements under Article 223 quinquies C apply to qualifying groups meeting statutory conditions, generally including a EUR 750 million consolidated revenue threshold for the relevant country-by-country reporting framework. Thresholds and entity scope must be tested under the applicable provisions for the fiscal year.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a general standalone regime formally called Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore regimes. French tax authorities may nevertheless challenge arrangements lacking commercial rationale or economic reality under domestic anti-abuse doctrines, including abuse of law, the principal-purpose test where applicable, transfer-pricing rules, permanent-establishment principles, and beneficial-ownership requirements. A French GDP clinical-logistics business should maintain evidence of real French personnel, premises, decision-making, regulated operational capacity, customer and supplier functions, and risk control consistent with its reported profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate tax evasion and fraudulent filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately concealing taxable income, fabricating expenses, using false invoices, maintaining undisclosed accounts, or submitting knowingly false tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessments, late-payment interest, and surcharges may apply. Individual tax fraud can carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine; aggravated cases can carry up to seven years and a EUR 3 million fine, subject to statutory conditions. Corporate criminal fines and additional penalties may apply, with amounts depending on the offence and the applicable legal provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face individual criminal liability where they personally participate in, direct, or knowingly facilitate the offence. Tax debt is not automatically transferred to directors, but statutory director-liability mechanisms may apply for fraudulent conduct or serious and repeated tax non-compliance. Imprisonment or travel restrictions require a legal basis and competent authority action; they are not automatic consequences of an assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing related-party freight, logistics, clinical-handling, management, financing, or IP transactions without arm's-length support; failing to provide required documentation; or shifting profits away from functions, assets, and risks located in France.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments, interest, and applicable surcharges may result. Failure to provide required transfer-pricing documentation may trigger a specific fine, generally the greater of EUR 10,000 or 0.5% of the relevant transactions, subject to statutory limits and conditions; additional consequences may apply for understated tax or incomplete responses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be exposed for personal participation in fraud or other separately established misconduct. Routine transfer-pricing adjustments do not by themselves pierce the corporate veil or automatically create personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Concealed permanent establishment or artificial profit allocation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using personnel, dependent agents, warehouses, or operational sites to conduct French business while omitting a taxable French presence or allocating profits inconsistently with actual functions and control of risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unreported French taxable profits may be assessed with interest and applicable surcharges. Criminal sanctions require proof of a separately defined offence, such as fraud; an incorrect treaty or permanent-establishment position alone does not automatically constitute a criminal offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability may arise only under applicable statutory or criminal rules based on the director's conduct. It is not automatic merely because a permanent establishment is found.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper dividend, royalty, or interest withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a treaty reduction or exemption without valid residence, beneficial-ownership, ownership, or other eligibility evidence; failing to withhold or remit tax; or mischaracterizing a distribution as interest, royalty, or service income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The French payer may be assessed for unpaid withholding tax, interest, and applicable surcharges. The precise consequences depend on the payment type, the recipient's status, and the failure involved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company is ordinarily the withholding agent. A director may face personal or criminal consequences only where statutory conditions for personal liability or participation in an offence are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fraudulent company dissolution or asset diversion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Diverting company assets, making sham distributions, or arranging insolvency or liquidation to defeat tax creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil recovery, insolvency proceedings, tax reassessment, and criminal penalties may apply depending on the conduct. French law does not impose an automatic general travel ban or imprisonment solely for unpaid corporate tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director may face civil liability under applicable tax, company, or insolvency law where statutory conditions are met, including fraudulent conduct or serious and repeated breaches. Veil-piercing, restitution, restrictions on management, or criminal punishment require a specific legal basis and competent decision.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: GDP, customs, and pharmaceutical logistics non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating regulated pharmaceutical distribution or clinical-logistics activities without required authorizations, falsifying GDP records, mishandling temperature-controlled products, or misdeclaring goods, origin, value, or customs classification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory measures may include inspections, corrective orders, suspension or withdrawal of authorization, product or shipment holds, customs reassessments, administrative fines, and criminal sanctions where the relevant offence is established. Tax penalties may additionally apply to false customs or accounting records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for offences they commit or knowingly facilitate, and may face separate regulatory or criminal consequences under applicable pharmaceutical, customs, and company law. A license breach does not automatically make directors liable for all corporate debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing beneficial owners, processing proceeds of crime, making prohibited payments, or failing to comply with applicable sanctions and reporting obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties depend on the specific AML, sanctions, or criminal-law breach and may include substantial fines, confiscation, regulatory restrictions, and imprisonment for criminal offences. A general corporate AML reporting duty should not be inferred without confirming that the SAS is a regulated obliged entity or otherwise subject to the relevant requirement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal or regulatory liability for their own participation, authorization, or legally relevant failure to act. Travel restrictions and imprisonment are not automatic and require an applicable legal basis and procedure.
